title: Resume injection orients Claude correctly regardless of what caused the restart

brief.done: After a self-caused bridge restart, Claude's first response demonstrates correct orientation — references its own prior action as the likely cause rather than treating the restart as an unexplained external event. After an external restart, message correctly frames it as external. Tests updated.
brief.what: 1. Identify the three restart scenarios the message must handle: intentional (user-triggered restart/deploy), self-caused (Claude's own actions triggered it), and crash (bridge died unexpectedly) 2. Determine whether the bridge can distinguish these cases at resume time — check what state survives in sse-sessions.json or could be added (e.g. last-prompt-text, shutdown-reason) 3. Rewrite the injection text for each case, or write a single neutral version that doesn't assume external agency — e.g. 'Your session was interrupted and has been resumed. Your last action may have caused this.' 4. If distinguishable: tailor the message (self-caused: 'You triggered a bridge restart — review your recent actions'; external: 'The bridge was restarted externally'; crash: 'The bridge crashed and recovered') 5. Update the deliverPrompt call at bridge.ts:954-956 and corresponding test expectations in state-builder.test.ts
brief.why: Current resume prompt says 'The bridge was restarted and your session has been resumed' — framing the restart as an external event that happened TO Claude. But often Claude itself caused the restart (e.g. systemctl restart during deployment work). The passive framing creates a phantom-limb effect: Claude looks outward for context instead of recognising its own agency in the restart. This misorientation wastes the first turn and can cause Claude to re-investigate things it already resolved.

title: Field Report: gueridon session lifecycle is an implicit state machine — new-session launch and Desktop-session control both leak hidden state

brief.done: gueridon models the session lifecycle as an explicit state machine with navigation / session-kind / billing-mode as separate axes: launching a new session in ANY billing mode always starts fresh from the lobby; a lingering Desktop/local session is clearable (or clearly labelled observe-only + how to clear) from the UI. Verified by reproducing both original symptoms and confirming they resolve.
brief.how:
Needs a gueridon-focused session with the code loaded (and mind the LIVE gueridon session in the roster - do not step on it). Verify against the code whether session/navigation/billing state is a single mutable blob vs separate concerns; the 'exit to lobby' manual escape hatch is the tell that transitions are not modelled. Reconcile with whatever 'completed-session-blocking' fix already shipped - it may be only the RC-half of this. This is a 'one unstated model behind many fiddly symptoms' case: decide the model, do not patch the symptoms. Proposed abstraction - an explicit lifecycle state machine with enumerated states (lobby / launching / in-session / ended-or-stale) and legal transitions, separating THREE axes so they cannot cross-contaminate: (a) navigation (lobby vs in-session); (b) session kind (RC-launched = controllable vs Desktop/local = observe-only); (c) billing mode (a launch PARAMETER, never a navigation mutator). Consequences: 'new session' always transitions FROM lobby regardless of prior current-session; selecting Vertex/Teams/Fable sets a launch param without changing where you are; the roster renders per-kind affordances (End for RC; for local either a host-side SIGTERM action or at minimum a clear observe-only / clear-on-host label).

SALVAGE-BEFORE-RESTART (added 2026-07-19, node-22 restart): restarting the bridge with live sessions in the cgroup (KillMode=control-group) SIGTERMs every one, and there is no first-class way to rescue them - it took a manual UUID-archaeology dig. Sameer flagged this as the real gap ('sorting out those handoffs properly'). The manual recipe that worked: RC sessions do NOT carry --session-id in the cmdline and do NOT hold the JSONL fd open between turns, so recover each UUID by matching the process start-time (ps -o lstart, BST) to each candidate ~/.claude/projects/<enc>/<uuid>.jsonl's first-entry timestamp (UTC, so subtract 1h); then `claude --resume <uuid>` in a LOGIN shell (runs under user@.service, so it SURVIVES the cgroup restart), ending the bridge's copy first (kill <pid>, graceful) to honour the one-driver invariant. The first-class fix this implies is a third roster verb beyond observe/control: SALVAGE - the roster exposes each live session's resume command (show/copy, or a one-tap detach-to-terminal) so a restart never costs a dig. Belongs in the same lifecycle model: 'salvage' is a legal transition from in-session (bridge-owned) to observe-only (handed to a login shell).
brief.what: Two repros as evidence. SYMPTOM 1 - cannot End a Desktop/local session, does not auto-clear: a completed batterie-de-savoir session lingered as grey 'local . 12h' with NO End button and blocked starting a new batterie session. It was a Desktop/local-agent session (claude agents --json showed state=None) with a live lingering process; gueridon can observe local sessions but offers no End, and 'claude kill <id>' refuses them (No job matching - it only manages RC-launched jobs). Cleared by host-side kill -TERM <pid> on tube (graceful; SessionEnd hooks ran; dropped from roster 7->6). So the shipped 'completed-session-blocking' fix appears to cover only RC sessions gueridon controls, not Desktop sessions with lingering processes. SYMPTOM 2 - new-session-as-Vertex dropped into the PREVIOUS session: selecting a new session with Vertex billing routed into the existing/previous session view instead of a fresh launch; escape required press-and-hold on the context-% indicator -> 'exit to lobby', after which a new session could start. Hypothesis: the new-session action's behaviour depends on hidden current-session state and billing-mode selection is entangled with navigation state.
brief.why: Two session-lifecycle bugs surfaced in real mobile use (2026-07-13, Sameer). They share ONE root: gueridon's session state is implicit/scattered rather than an explicit state machine, so concerns that should be orthogonal (navigation, session-kind, billing-mode) leak into each other. Left unfixed, launching and managing sessions from mobile stays fiddly and untrustworthy - the exact thing gueridon exists to make smooth - and each symptom gets patched individually instead of the model being fixed. Sameer's own read: 'janky state machine, might need abstracting out' - agreed.

done_note: Superseded by outcome gdn-ruvegu (2026-07-19 /plan). This Field Report bundled 5 things; the substrate-watch check redistributed them: Symptom 1 (End a local session) -> gdn-racuca DONE + deployed today; Symptom 2 (Vertex-new-drops-into-old) -> gdn-duhino; adopt/graduate-to-terminal -> gdn-pizoke; billing-labelling -> gdn-kozoha; the salvage UUID-archaeology -> OBSOLETE (claude agents --json now hands you the sessionId); the 'explicit state machine' abstraction -> kept as the three-axis FRAME in understanding.md, NOT a refactor (substrate removed the symptoms that justified one). No work lost; better scoped.

title: Tool chips flow like Tetris blocks, filling available width before wrapping

brief.done: On a 390px-wide screen, consecutive collapsed tool chips pack horizontally like Tetris blocks — short chips sit side-by-side, long ones take a full row, and the layout re-flows on orientation change. Expanded chips remain full-width.
brief.what: The chip-grid already has flex-wrap:wrap and chips are inline-flex — the wrapping infrastructure is correct. The real issue is that individual chips are wide enough to fill a 390px row on their own. Each chip contains: status icon + tool name (white-space:nowrap) + path (max-width:100px) + hidden detail div. On a 390px screen with 14px message padding, available width is ~362px. A typical chip with a path is ~160-180px — two barely fit, three never do. Steps: 1. Reduce .c-path max-width from 100px to ~60px (paths are already ellipsized, less width still readable) 2. Consider adding max-width to .chip itself (e.g. max-width:45%) so chips are forced to share rows 3. Verify that expanded chips still get flex-basis:100% and render full-width 4. Test on 390px viewport: consecutive Read, Edit, Bash chips should pack 2-3 per row
brief.why: The design intent for collapsed tool chips was Tetris-like packing — chips fill horizontal space and wrap to the next line when full, re-flowing on resize. Currently most chips stack one-per-line like a vertical list, wasting horizontal space. Only occasionally do two chips sit side-by-side (visible in screenshot where two Read chips share a row). The layout should be flex-wrap or inline-block so chips pack tightly regardless of screen width.

title: Guéridon runs one instance per person behind the atelier's front door: unix-socket listen, identity guard, roster without the Teams lane

brief.done: On the atelier, https://atelier-door-334414659111.europe-west2.run.app opens Guéridon's launcher for the signed-in person; a prompt spawns claude under their uid (ps -o user); curl --unix-socket with a missing or mismatched X-Atelier-User gets 403; the roster lists only that person's sessions while another user's claude process is running; npm test green.
brief.how: Design note: docs/atelier-per-user.md. Listen: honour systemd socket activation (LISTEN_FDS, fd 3) first, then BRIDGE_SOCKET=<path> (unlink stale, chmod 0666: the 0750 directory is the wall, and a user process cannot chgrp to frontdoor), else BRIDGE_PORT as now. Identity: when GUERIDON_REQUIRE_USER is set, every request must carry X-Atelier-User (name overridable by GUERIDON_USER_HEADER) equal to it, else 403 and a request:rejected event; missing header is a refusal too (deny by default). title: Vertex launches always start fresh, never silently resume the previous session

brief.done: Launching a Vertex session for a repo that has a prior session starts a FRESH session (new session-id, empty conversation), never silently resuming; deliberately returning to an existing session still resumes. brief.how: Root cause (verified this session, understanding.md 'Key seams'): launch.html launchVertex() does `location.href = '/#'+selected` — a bare hash nav carrying NO fresh-vs-resume intent. The conversation page (index.html) auto-connects from location.hash and the bridge's resolveSessionForFolder (bridge-logic.ts) resolves to RESUME whatever that folder last had. So 'new Vertex' == 'navigate to folder' == 'resume'. FIX = thread ONE bit of intent (fresh) from the launcher through the hash to session resolution — do NOT build a state machine. Likely shape: launcher writes `/#owner/repo?new` (or a sentinel) on a fresh Vertex launch; index.html parses it and asks the bridge for a fresh session (POST /session with a new --session-id, no --resume) rather than the default resume. MIND structural-lesson #1: the hash folder name is RAW (slash intact, never encodeURIComponent) — keep the intent bit separate from the folder name so the raw-match still works. Reproduce the symptom first (launch a repo, exit to lobby, re-launch Vertex on the same repo -> confirm it resumes not fresh) before fixing; add a unit test around the intent-carrying (launch.html inline JS is the untested blind spot — gdn-pefipi).
brief.what: 1. Reproduce Symptom 2 against the live UI (or a css-shell harness): fresh Vertex launch on a repo with a prior session resumes instead of starting fresh. 2. Decide the intent-carrying mechanism (hash query/sentinel vs an explicit /session param) that keeps the RAW folder-name match intact. 3. Implement: launcher signals 'new'; index.html + bridge honour it with a fresh --session-id, no --resume. 4. Preserve resume-on-purpose (returning to an existing session still resumes). 5. Test: a regression covering fresh-vs-resume intent through the seam.
brief.why: Symptom 2 from gdn-cepalu (live 2026-07-13): selecting a NEW session with Vertex billing dropped into the PREVIOUS session's view; escape needed a press-and-hold on the context-% -> 'exit to lobby'. title: Replace hand-rolled markdown renderer with marked

brief.done: All Claude markdown patterns render correctly including blockquotes and nested lists. Hand-rolled md() and inline() functions deleted. marked.umd.js served by bridge and loaded via script tag. No double-escaping issues. Existing CSS works, new blockquote/hr styles added.
brief.what: 1. SERVE MARKED — The bridge serves static files via a lookup table (bridge.ts:1028-1037). Add an entry to serve marked's UMD bundle: '/marked.js': {file: 'node_modules/marked/lib/marked.umd.js', mime: 'application/javascript'}. Add a tag in index.html before the main
brief.why: Hand-rolled md() function (index.html:1762-1884, ~120 lines) and inline() helper (index.html:1749-1758) cover a subset of markdown: headers, code blocks, tables, task lists, ordered/unordered lists, paragraphs, and inline formatting (bold, italic, strikethrough, code, links). Missing: blockquotes (Claude does emit these — confirmed by user), nested lists, horizontal rules, images, reference links. Each missing pattern silently falls through to paragraph rendering, producing incorrect output. marked (v17, already installed as dep — package.json) is zero transitive deps, 42KB UMD bundle, handles full GFM including all missing patterns.

steps: SERVE MARKED — The bridge serves static files via a lookup table (bridge.ts:1028-1037). Add an entry to serve marked's UMD bundle: '/marked.js': {file: 'node_modules/marked/lib/marked.umd.js', mime: 'application/javascript'}. Add a <script src='/marked.js'></script> tag in index.html before the main <script> block.

REPLACE md() — Delete the md() function (index.html:1762-1884) and inline() function (index.html:1749-1758). Replace all md(text) calls with marked.parse(text). marked.parse() returns HTML string, same as md() did. Find call sites by searching for 'md(' in the script section.
REPLACE inline() — Search for inline() calls outside of md(). These are used for rendering snippets that need inline formatting but not block-level parsing. Replace with marked.parseInline(text).

CONFIGURE MARKED — Set options for our use case: marked.setOptions({gfm: true, breaks: false}). GFM enables tables, task lists, strikethrough. breaks:false means single newlines don't become
(matches current md() behaviour where newlines within paragraphs are collapsed).

SANITIZATION — The current md() calls esc() first (HTML entity encoding) before processing. marked handles its own escaping — do NOT double-escape. Remove any esc() calls that wrap marked input. marked's output is safe for innerHTML by default (it escapes HTML in markdown source).

CSS — Existing .msg-assistant styles (index.html:87-158) target p, strong, em, code, pre, ul, ol, li, table, th, td. marked's output uses the same standard HTML elements, so styles should work without changes. Add styles for blockquote (.msg-assistant blockquote) and hr (.msg-assistant hr) since these were never needed before. Suggested: blockquote gets left border in --text-dim, slight indent, dimmed text. hr gets border-color: var(--border).
TEST PATTERNS — After replacement, verify these render correctly: (a) # Header, (b) **bold** and *italic*, (c) , (d) | tables |, (e) - [x] task lists, (f) > blockquotes (the new one), (g)
ordered lists, (h) --- horizontal rules, (i) [links](url), (j) nested lists.

title: Design pass: wallet and surface model on top of the existing launcher roster

brief.done: gdn-jibudu has a reviewed design and a set of build actions; Sameer has seen the design and his --badly clauses each map to a design decision.
brief.how:
Read gdn-jibudu's brief first (mechanism facts + Sameer's verbatim --badly). Design questions: how a roster row learns its wallet (read CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR from /proc environ in scanClaudeSessions, like vertexBilled already does); how the launcher offers a wallet at launch (a third dimension beside the Vertex|Teams buttons, or a picker); how cross-wallet resume enforces --fork-session in buildCCArgs; where per-wallet 429/reset state lives. Constraint from CLAUDE.md: the streaming lane is maintenance-mode — extend the roster/launch surfaces, not the stream-json layer.

DESIGN INPUT 2026-08-28 (from the teleport-id session on tube). Sameer, verbatim: "I've been feeling the need for a 'switchboard' that can 'see' all my claude sessions - certainly all Code ones, but perhaps going broader than that to Vertex sessions, plus maybe even Cowork as that's CC in a straitjacket... crucially allowing me to pick up a session from one interface to another for the remaining gaps... For instance - Vertex spawned Gueridon session that i want to open in Ghostty or whatever. Needs care working through the different permutations (state machine?)."

THE FRAME: the roster is PID-KEYED; the switchboard needs a UUID-KEYED layer underneath it. buildSessionRoster scans /proc, so it sees only what is alive, only on this host, and loses a session entirely when its process dies. A session's durable identity is its UUID — the thing --resume takes and the thing the JSONL is named for. Every capability in gdn-jibudu's --what is an operation on that second layer, with liveness demoted to an attribute of a session rather than the index.

HANDLE TABLE — what each surface's UI actually hands the user, and whether it maps to a local UUID:
- local TUI (Ghostty/tmux): the UUID itself. Direct.
- Remote Control / iOS app / Claude Desktop: ONLY a teleport id (session_...). EDGE CLOSED 2026-08-28 — uuid5("3ab19d7e-9f35-45c2-926e-75e271cc60b3", "https://api.anthropic.com/v1/code/sessions/cse_<body>"), namespace and URL name-form read out of the CC bundle. trousse 1.78.1 ships scripts/teleport-id.sh (handle -> uuid, computed, works offline and at any age) and scripts/remote-sessions.sh (lists them). Related: these sessions carry a version-5 UUID and never get an ai-title, which is exactly why they are absent from the --resume picker.
- Gueridon-spawned: UUID already tracked (folders.ts:50). Direct.
- Vertex terminal (claudev/claudefv): UUID. Direct; the roster already labels the kind.
- Cowork (Desktop): UNKNOWN. OPEN QUESTION to settle before promising "all my sessions" — where do its transcripts land, and does it produce a resumable local JSONL at all?
- claude.ai chats: no resume concept. The overnight importer gives read-only history; keep them OUT of the state machine and show them, if at all, as archive.

WHY TODAY'S EDGE IS THE PIECE THAT WAS MISSING: gdn-kidowe (dropped 2026-07-11) documented the reverse direction as "a manual `claude --resume <id>` at the desk". For Remote-Control sessions that manual path did not actually exist — Desktop exposes only session_..., and nothing mapped it to a local UUID. The documented escape hatch was unavailable in precisely the lane that needed it. It now works.

THREE STATES (the state machine he gestured at):
- COLD: JSONL on disk, no live holder. Any surface may resume. The common case, and the one a pid-keyed roster cannot see at all.
- HELD-LOCAL: a live pid holds it. Handoff = gdn-kidowe's verified path — SIGTERM (graceful exit is a faithful /exit; hooks fire, JSONL flushes) then force-resume the explicit id.
- HELD-REMOTE: a cloud worker holds the lease; no SIGTERM available. Either fork, or archive first — the bridge speaks POST /v1/sessions/<session_...>/archive (seen in ~/.claude/logs/claude-remote-*.log).
Plus gdn-jibudu's standing rule: cross-WALLET resume always forks.

DO NOT REDISCOVER — the kidowe seam: a graceful exit may write a bon handoff for that session id, and resolveSessionForFolder treats handoffSessionId === latestSessionFile.id as "start FRESH", which would LOSE the conversation on takeover. Takeover must force-resume the explicit id, bypassing that guard. Already written up in gdn-kidowe's brief; do not re-derive it.

CROSS-HOST is a real permutation, not an edge case: "all my sessions" spans tube and the Mac, each with its own ~/.claude/projects. The roster is machine-local and the overnight importer is a snapshot, not a live view. Decide early whether the switchboard is per-host with a federated view, or one host reading the others.

CHECKED, NO ACTION NEEDED: gueridon only ever encodes paths (folders.ts:79, non-alnum -> "-") and never decodes them, so it does NOT carry the one-way-decode bug fixed in trousse today.

SCOPE QUESTION FOR SAMEER, still open at filing time: gdn-jibudu's brief scopes the switchboard as "NOT a universal remote that drives tmux/Desktop/phone surfaces", and gdn-kidowe was consciously shelved. Cross-surface HANDOFF is adjacent to that exclusion rather than identical to it. Asked 2026-08-28: fold into gdn-jibudu, revive kidowe, or a sibling outcome?

COWORK OPEN QUESTION — ANSWERED 2026-08-28 (measured on tube, CC 2.1.250, Desktop store present). Local Cowork IS fully addressable; it is the easiest surface of the lot, not the hardest.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY DOES: Cowork is Claude Code writing into the ordinary transcript farm, plus a Desktop-side sidecar index. There is no separate transcript format and no separate location.
- Farm side: ~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd>/<uuid>.jsonl, entrypoint "claude-desktop" (a third value beside "cli" and "sdk-cli"). 21 such sessions on tube. All 21 carry a version-4 uuid and a real .cwd — structurally identical to a terminal session.
- Sidecar: ~/.config/Claude/claude-code-sessions/<accountId>/<workspaceId>/local_<uuid>.json. Keys: sessionId (the "local_..." id, which is what Cowork's own handoffs cite — see bon's candidate-mode notes), cliSessionId, cwd, originCwd, title, titleSource, model, effort, isArchived, permissionMode, enabledMcpTools, lastActivityAt.
- THE EDGE: sidecar.cliSessionId IS the farm uuid. Measured 21/21 resolve to a real transcript on disk. So Cowork's own id maps to a resumable uuid by a file read — no derivation needed, unlike the teleport lane.

RESUMABLE: yes, verified end-to-end rather than inferred. `claude --resume <uuid> --fork-session -p ...` on a claude-desktop session recovered its true first prompt (not "NO HISTORY"), and the original transcript was left byte-identical (53646B, mtime unchanged) because the fork wrote elsewhere. --fork-session is the right probe for any resumability test: it proves the history loads without touching the original, which matters when the original may still have a live holder.

THE USEFUL ASYMMETRY FOR THE SWITCHBOARD: these transcripts carry NO ai-title and NO slug — 0/21, against 24/25 for "cli" sessions in the same window — so Cowork sessions are nameless in `claude --resume` exactly like teleport sessions are. But the sidecar HAS a human title ("Mawitu pickup", "Tube RDP setup issues", "Network performance diagnosis"). So the switchboard can show good names for Cowork rows for free, by reading the sidecar, where the CLI picker shows nothing. Same trick does not exist for teleport sessions, whose title is server-side only (it can be scraped from the bridge log's "derived title for session_..." line).

STILL OPEN, do not assume: CLOUD Cowork is a different surface (Firecracker microVM, ephemeral $HOME — see trousse skill-forge references/cowork-cloud.md), so it almost certainly leaves no local transcript on tube, but that is reasoned, NOT measured. ~/.config/Claude/claude-code-vm/2.1.229 exists and hints at that lane. Also unmeasured: multi-account and multi-workspace nesting — only one accountId and one workspaceId dir exist here, so the sidecar path shape above is a sample of one at each level.

title: A tool-permission prompt under Guéridon is provoked deliberately and its rendering decided: refused-and-shown, or answerable from the phone

brief.done: A Guéridon session asked to use a disallowed tool shows the person what was refused and why, or lets them allow it from the phone; measured on the atelier through the door.
brief.how:
Provoke one on purpose: a prompt that needs a tool outside the allow list (WebFetch is disallowed today) and read what CC emits on stream-json (is there a permission_denied event, or just prose?). Then decide: render the refusal visibly in the conversation with the tool name, or wire --permission-prompt-tool to an AskUser-shaped overlay so the phone can answer. Check docs/CC-EVENTS.md and docs/empirical-verification.md for what is already known before measuring.

OPTION FROM OTODOCK (2026-09-12, read of github.com/OtoDock/oto-dock 1.6.0, clone at github.com/OtoDock/oto-dock at commit 39af5ff (release 1.6.0, 2026-09-09; permalink form github.com/OtoDock/oto-dock/blob/39af5ff/<path>#L<n>)): a hook CAN be the human gate, despite carte-jegise (a hook returning ask never renders a dialog). OtoDock runs claude -p with --dangerously-skip-permissions plus --permission-prompt-tool stdio, and its PreToolUse hook (proxy/hooks/permission_gate.py) does not return ask: it BLOCKS, long-polling the platform with a hook timeout of 604800 s (a week), until a human taps allow or deny in the dashboard, then returns that verdict. Transport loss fails closed, with a short retry ladder. For Guéridon that is the phone-side answer path: goûteur (or a bridge hook) parks the call, pushes the tool name and input to the phone, waits for the tap. Two facts to carry into step 1: (a) the presence of --permission-prompt-tool stdio is what restores AskUserQuestion to a headless roster — measured 2026-09-09 on tube, CC 2.1.267, 0 vs 1 with only that flag changed (aboyeur aby-tevina has the worker-side twin); (b) OtoDock keeps the stdio channel silent and has the hook deny AskUserQuestion while forwarding the question, because in bypass mode a real prompt routed to stdio would hang with nothing answering. Edit/NotebookEdit validate their target BEFORE PreToolUse runs, so a hook cannot rewrite their paths (permission_gate.py _path_note) — irrelevant to the gate, relevant if the bridge ever translates paths.

CORRECTION 2026-09-12 (review verifier): Step 1 is already half-answered in docs/empirical-verification.md:215-232: a --disallowedTools tool is removed from the model's view entirely, so provoking with WebFetch emits NO event and the model never attempts it; permission_denials only shows post-hoc in the result event. The real probe is a tool the model can see but the allow rules don't cover (e.g. a Bash command outside the rules) under --permission-mode default, and the phone-answerable route is --permission-prompt-tool; measurement should start there.

title: CC --resume with missing session file produces no init event — silent 30s hang

With the mcpServers fix in place, --resume with a missing session may now work correctly. However, the defensive improvements described in --what are still valuable: pre-checking session existence before choosing --resume, and parsing stderr for fast-fail detection.

title: Vertex sessions toggle between terminal and phone via a clean baton-pass

brief.done: Tapping a live Vertex terminal session in the roster continues THAT conversation on the phone (same sessionId, full history), with the terminal session cleanly ended; no two-driver JSONL collision.
brief.how:
Takeover path: roster tap on a foreign Vertex terminal session → confirm ('this ends the terminal session and continues it here') → Guéridon SIGTERMs the foreign pid (the verified graceful-exit = faithful /exit, SessionEnd hooks fire, JSONL flushes, --resume-able; same mechanism as DELETE /launch RC End) → resume it as Guéridon's own -p Vertex session (/#folder). SEAM TO SOLVE: a graceful exit may write a bon handoff for that session-id, and resolveSessionForFolder treats 'handoffSessionId === latestSessionFile.id → start FRESH', which would LOSE the conversation on takeover — the takeover must force-resume the specific id, bypassing that guard. Reverse (phone→terminal) is a manual `claude --resume <id>` at the desk — Guéridon can't spawn a terminal; document the asymmetry. Depends on gdn (honest Vertex roster label) landing first so the tap target exists.

REVIVED 2026-08-28 as gdn-merozu (under gdn-jibudu), on Sameer's one-word 'revive'. This item stays DONE/dropped — it is not reopened; gdn-merozu supersedes and widens it from Vertex terminal<->phone to cross-surface handoff generally. What unblocked it: the reverse direction documented here as 'a manual claude --resume <id> at the desk' was not actually available for Remote Control sessions, because those surfaces expose only a teleport id and nothing mapped it to a local UUID. That derivation was found in the CC bundle on 2026-08-28 and ships in trousse 1.78.1. The SIGTERM/force-resume path and the resolveSessionForFolder fresh-start seam written up here are still the live design and are cited by gdn-merozu — read them there rather than re-deriving.
brief.what: 1. POST /takeover/:folder → SIGTERM foreign pid, wait for clean exit, resume as -p 2. force-resume that bypasses the handoff/exit fresh-start guard for an explicit takeover 3. confirm UI on the roster row 4. asymmetry documented (phone→terminal is manual) 5. tests: takeover resolves to the SAME sessionId; handoff-guard bypass covered
brief.why: Sameer wants to move a Vertex session back and forth between his terminal (claudefv) and Guéridon on the phone — 'I was hoping I could just toggle back and forth'. A simultaneous live mirror is impossible (two processes, one JSONL, corruption), but a baton-pass (one live driver at a time, handed off cleanly) is not. This is the real answer to the 'join existing Vertex sessions even if not Guéridon-launched' ask; parked at 'tickle only' appetite (2026-07-09), streaming lane is in maintenance mode.

title: Bridge sends text/current/state instead of delta events

brief.done: Bridge emits text+current+state events. Old delta events still emitted in parallel (transition safety). No client changes yet — new events are ignored by old client (SSE spec: unknown events = no-op).
brief.what: 1. In handleCCEvent, after stateBuilder.handleEvent(), check signal type and broadcast new events alongside old deltas 2. text signal → broadcastToSession('text', {append: newText}) — triggered by conflation flush. REUSE the existing deltaFlushInterval timer pattern for batching. 3. structure signal → broadcastToSession('current', stateBuilder.getCurrentMessage()) — tool_start, tool_complete, thinking, inner API call 4. status/ask_user unchanged (status rides on current message, ask_user stays separate) 5. Turn-end state broadcast unchanged. TRAPS: (a) getCurrentMessage() returns near-empty {text:null, tool_calls:[], thinking:null, activity:null} between system:init and first content_block_start — treat as 'working, no content yet' (show spinner, don't send empty message). (b) After handleAssistant commits to state.messages but before result, the last message in getState().messages and getCurrentMessage() describe the SAME message — naive [...messages, currentMessage] would duplicate it. Gate on currentMessagePushed or compare.
brief.why: The bridge currently broadcasts SSEDelta objects as 'delta' SSE events. The new protocol has three event types: 'text' (append string for streaming tokens), 'current' (full replacement of the streaming message on structural changes), and 'state' (full snapshot at turn end, same as now). The conflation timer stays — it gates text events. CRITICAL: during transition, send BOTH old deltas AND new events so the client can be switched independently.

title: Revive the baton-pass: pick a session up on another surface

brief.badly: The model gets confused - gear slips in the environment that mess with the coherence of context or fail to give awareness of important transition characteristics, and I get confused too - not knowing in under 20s how to pick up the session where I was noodling something about XXX on surface YYY. (Sameer, verbatim, 2026-08-29)
brief.done: From the phone, Sameer can take a session that is running anywhere — Guéridon, a Vertex terminal, or spawned from the iOS app — and either continue it where he is or be handed the exact one-line command to continue it in Ghostty, with the previous holder cleanly released and the transcript intact. A session whose process has already exited is just as actionable as a live one.
brief.how:
READ FIRST, do not re-derive: gdn-kidowe's brief (the SIGTERM-then-force-resume path and the seam below) and the DESIGN INPUT paragraph appended to gdn-himaba on 2026-08-28 (handle table per surface, the three states, cross-host question). THE SEAM THAT WILL BITE: a graceful exit may write a bon handoff for that session id, and resolveSessionForFolder treats handoffSessionId === latestSessionFile.id as 'start FRESH' — a takeover that does not force-resume the explicit id SILENTLY LOSES the conversation. THE STRUCTURAL MOVE: buildSessionRoster is pid-keyed, so it sees only what is alive on this host and loses a session when its process dies. Handoff needs a UUID-keyed layer underneath, with liveness demoted to an attribute. THREE STATES: COLD (JSONL on disk, no holder — any surface may resume; the roster is blind to these); HELD-LOCAL (a live pid — SIGTERM gives a faithful /exit, hooks fire, JSONL flushes, then force-resume the explicit id); HELD-REMOTE (a cloud worker holds the lease, no pid to signal — fork, or archive first via POST /v1/sessions/<session_...>/archive, which the bridge already speaks). Standing rule from gdn-jibudu, unchanged: cross-WALLET resume always forks. ASYMMETRY TO KEEP HONEST: Guéridon cannot spawn a terminal, so phone->Ghostty is 'show me the exact command to paste', not a button — that is a legitimate and useful rung, not a failure. Do not build a terminal-spawner to avoid admitting it. Constraint from CLAUDE.md: the streaming lane is maintenance-mode — extend the roster/launch surfaces, not the stream-json layer.

DESIGN PASS 2026-08-29 (gdn-himaba): docs/switchboard-design.md — the pickup flow is this item's territory (build 3): wallet sheet on a RECENT row -> force-resume the explicit uuid under the chosen spawn env, --fork-session whenever the wallet differs from last-observed, and bypass the resolveSessionForFolder fresh-on-handoff guard (kidowe seam). Blocked on Sameer's --badly. The gdn-vutogu spike (RC --resume) decides whether pickup can also land in the phone-native app.

FROM THE --badly (2026-08-29): the 'gear slips' half implies a TRANSITION PREAMBLE — every pickup injects a [gueridon:transition]-style note telling the resumed model what changed: previous surface -> new surface, previous wallet -> new wallet, host, and elapsed gap. The human half sets a hard budget: topic-memory -> running session in under 20 seconds (search + tap + lane pick).

SPIKE VERDICT (gdn-vutogu, 2026-08-30, measured under hublot): claude --remote-control <name> --resume <uuid> --fork-session WORKS on a cold session - history replayed, /remote-control active with a fresh claude.ai/code/session_ URL, Teams:sameer billing, original transcript byte-identical, no turn run at spawn (zero quota). So the wallet sheet can offer TWO destinations for Teams-seat pickups: Gueridon UI (streaming -p, any wallet) or send-to-claude.ai (RC flag form; lands on whichever account the spawn env's config dir holds - viewer needs that account's web bookmark). Vertex pickups remain Gueridon-UI-only (RC hard-refuses Vertex). Docs also show an in-session route: /remote-control slash command inside any live TUI session.

SCOPE NOTE 2026-09-09: the 'handing over is not remote-driving' line stands for THIS item (hand-off is still the route for continuing a session on the phone), but gdn-jibudu's exclusion of remote-driving was reversed the same day for the bounded dialog-answer case — see the REVERSAL paragraph on gdn-jibudu. Two different rungs: answer-a-dialog stays in place; pick-up-and-continue moves the session.

FACT 2026-09-09 (measured, 2.1.266): claude --resume's picker FILTERS OUT every sdk-cli/sdk-ts/sdk-py session by design ('filtered from /resume: entrypoint=' in the bundle; live hublot probe in ~ showed no row for a 27-min-old phone session, 'adhd' → No sessions match). So a phone session can only ever be picked up by explicit uuid — which makes deliverable 4 (hand the exact command to a terminal) the ONLY terminal route, not a convenience. title: Idle clientless sessions get reaped without waiting for a bridge restart

brief.done: A session whose client vanishes via a half-open socket (no clean disconnect) has its CC process reaped within a bounded idle window, no bridge restart needed.
brief.how: Add a periodic sweep (e.g. alongside the 30s ping loop at bridge.ts:1655) that arms maybeStartGraceTimer on every clientless session, or kills sessions whose lastOutputTime/lastPromptAt exceed an idle threshold. Also add server-side dead-client detection (the 30s ping can't detect a half-open socket; it only cleans up when res.write throws) or aggressive TCP keepalive. Relates to gdn-jevico, gdn-cuduci. FUTURE B (2026-06-29): RC sessions in the rcSessions map are processes too and need the same idle reaping — but note pty.kill() defaults to SIGHUP, which claude SURVIVES (observed: orphaned RC processes outlived pty.kill() in test harnesses). RC reaping must escalate SIGTERM→SIGKILL like killWithEscalation does for -p processes, not rely on SIGHUP. In prod the systemd KillMode=control-group covers bridge shutdown, but idle-reaping mid-life does not get that backstop.
brief.what: 1. Periodic idle-session sweep 2. Server-side dead-client detection (or aggressive keepalive) 3. Exit handler deletes process-dead sessions from the map (audit finding #11).
brief.why: Two real motivations, NEITHER is quota (idle sessions burn ZERO tokens — cost tracks turns only; confirmed 2026-06-29). (1) INVISIBILITY: an orphaned session has no surface anywhere — a vivid-vale session sat idle 3.7 days (PID 105337) unseen until manually reaped via /exit. (2) RELAUNCH COLLISION (elevated by the Future-B launcher, which makes multi-session-per-repo trivial): launching a NEW session in a repo whose previous one never /closed cleanly leaves two live CC processes in one CWD — hazardous because bon tactical state is CWD-keyed, so both sessions see and advance the SAME tactical (the open skill warns of exactly this desync). MECHANISM: the only thing that kills an idle session is a 5-min grace timer, armed solely on a clean client disconnect (detachFromSession/onTurnComplete). A half-open mobile/Tailscale SSE socket dies without firing res.on-close, so grace never starts and the claude -p process lives forever; the startup orphan-reaper only runs on restart. bridge.ts:291-321,1655.

done_note: Cut at 2026-07-07 triage: motivations self-eroded — idle sessions burn zero tokens, the roster (gdn-batogo) covers visibility, RC relaunch is idempotent per folder. Residual harm is ~440MB RSS per forgotten -p process until the next deploy. Revive on felt RAM pain.

title: init:timeout leaves zombie session in memory — reconnect loop

brief.done: Opening a folder after init:timeout no longer produces an infinite timeout loop — the user either sees a fresh session, an actionable error, or an automatic retry that converges.
brief.what: A decision on how to handle init:timeout cleanup. The loop: spawnCC sets resumable=true (bridge.ts ~L319) → CC hangs → init:timeout kills process (bridge.ts ~L325) but session stays in Map → resolveSessionForFolder sees existingBridgeSession → isReconnect:true → spawnCC with --resume → hangs again forever. Key locations: bridge.ts spawnCC() ~L297, init timeout ~L325, bridge-logic.ts resolveSessionForFolder() ~L220. Repro: open a project with slow MCP server or corrupt session state, wait for timeout, retry. Multiple valid fixes: (a) delete session from Map — silent fresh retry, (b) mark non-resumable but keep — same ID with --session-id not --resume, (c) surface error to user with Retry/Start Fresh choice, (d) retry counter with escalation after N failures. Consider: in the observed case (MCP needing uv dep resolution after config recovery) a fresh session would also have failed — surfacing the error may be better than silent retry. Also consider distinguishing transient failures (MCP slow) from permanent ones (corrupt state).

title: Input area overshoots behind status bar when keyboard appears

brief.done: Keyboard open/close leaves the input area at the bottom of the visible viewport. No overshoot behind the status bar. Works in both Safari and standalone, including emoji keyboard.
brief.what: 1. Investigate the race: the visualViewport resize event fires multiple times as the keyboard animates. The handler sets height on each fire — intermediate heights during animation could cause overshoot. 2. Consider debouncing the resize handler (requestAnimationFrame or 100ms debounce) so it only acts on the final viewport size. 3. Check whether window.scrollTo(0,0) is counterproductive — iOS automatically scrolls the focused element into view, and scrollTo(0,0) may be fighting it. Try removing the scrollTo. 4. Test in both Safari and standalone mode — the isStandalone branch has different logic. 5. Check if this only happens on certain screen sizes or keyboard types (emoji keyboard is taller).
brief.why: Sometimes when the iOS keyboard opens, the input area and messages scroll up too far — the input box ends up near or behind the status bar (signal strength, clock, battery). It doesn't happen every time, suggesting a race between the visualViewport resize handler and iOS layout. The current handler (index.html ~line 1156) sets html/body height to visualViewport.height when keyboard opens in standalone mode, and calls window.scrollTo(0,0). The scrollTo may be fighting iOS's own scroll-into-view behaviour for the focused input.

It's the SIGTERM-by-pid primitive (understanding.md observe-from-outside #1) — no pty handle needed. Client: launch.html roster rows for kind local/vertex-terminal get an End button -> confirm('End <name>? Resumable.') -> DELETE /session/:pid -> refreshSessions. Keep owned rc/vertex End paths untouched (DELETE /launch/:folder, POST /exit/:folder). Gate on GUERIDON_ENABLE_RC (same as /sessions). WATCH: launch.html inline JS is the untested blind spot (gdn-pefipi veiled, raw-hash scar class) — verify the client branch by live self-render + a real disposable-session endpoint smoke, not just unit tests.

Router wiring for DELETE /session/:pid, gated 3. launch.html: End button on foreign roster rows + confirm + refresh 4. Unit tests for the pid guard + endpoint shape 5. title: A phone-spawned session starts at the floor of the lane it arrived on, not the ceiling of the host

brief.done: A phone-spawned session shows the kill-switch set in its own environment, and the permission mode it starts in is one somebody chose and wrote down rather than one it inherited by accident.
brief.how:
Two separable pieces; the second is nearly free and should not wait for the first.

1. THE KILL-SWITCH (cheap, mechanical). The claude-remote@ unit should set CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_REFUSAL_FALLBACK in its own Environment= (or an EnvironmentFile) rather than relying on a login shell it never gets. Verify by reading .message.model transitions in a phone session's transcript, not just by checking for model_refusal_fallback system entries — CLAUDE.md records that recovering from a pause by hand leaves no entry at all. Note the open question underneath it: no flag has ever been recorded landing on the phone surface on a current binary, so whether it swaps at all is unmeasured. Setting the variable makes the question moot either way.

2. THE PERMISSION FLOOR (a decision, not a patch). Decide deliberately what mode a phone-spawned session should start in, and set it in the unit rather than inheriting whatever CC defaults to. The trade is real and it is Sameer's: 'auto' is what makes the phone useful one-handed, and a prompting mode on a surface with no good dialog rendering is worse than useless (cf. gdn-hopubi, which is about exactly that rendering). So the honest options are (a) leave auto and record WHY, with the threat model written down, (b) auto for read-shaped work and a narrower deny list for the destructive verbs, or (c) a floor that varies with how the session was spawned. Do not silently tighten it — a phone lane that starts refusing things mid-week reads as breakage.

CORRECTION 2026-10-25 (bon review verifier, ACTIVE): Step 1 is done in infra 13542bc, apart from the brief's verification from a real phone transcript's .message.model transitions, which has not been seen. What is left is step 2: Sameer writes down whether 'auto', which the phone app picks per session and the unit cannot override, is accepted, and why (infra claude-remote@.service:34-41 has the facts).
brief.what: 1. The refusal-fallback kill-switch present in the claude-remote@ unit's own environment, verified from a real phone session's transcript. 2. A recorded decision on the phone lane's permission floor — including 'auto, deliberately, for these reasons' if that is the answer.
brief.why:
Two facts already recorded separately in the corpus, never put side by side. (1) traps.md: phone-spawned sessions via the claude-remote@ fleet arrive in 'auto' permission mode (measured 2026-08-16) — the mode whose whole pitch is approving without asking. (2) CLAUDE.md, model-specific section: the fleet execs the binary WITHOUT a login shell, so those sessions do not inherit CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_REFUSAL_FALLBACK from ~/.dotfiles/shell/{bashrc,zshrc} and can still swap model silently on a safeguards flag, which is OFF everywhere else on this estate by Sameer's 2026-08-31 decision. So the remote surface is simultaneously the least supervised and the one that misses the estate's kill-switch, and both are accidents of how the unit launches rather than decisions anyone made.

The counter-design, found 2026-09-13 in a 2026-09-01 OpenClaw read that was never written up (full note ~/notes/handoffs/2026-09-13-openclaw-residue.md; clone ~/repos/third-party/openclaw, docs/channels/pairing.md:186-204, docs/gateway/security/index.md:820, docs/tools/exec-approvals.md:319-323). Three rules, none of which we hold: a degraded transport automatically mints the LIMITED profile and cannot be upgraded without reconfiguring the transport and issuing a fresh pairing code; a reconnecting device asking for wider scopes keeps its old approval and raises a separate pending upgrade, so nothing widens silently; and KILL-SWITCHES MUST NOT LIVE IN INHERITABLE ENV — they blocked their whole OPENCLAW_* namespace from untrusted workspace .env files precisely so a future control is fail-closed rather than silently inheritable. Ours is exactly such a variable, and the phone lane is exactly the place it goes missing.

VERDICT: watch, not act — this is doctrine read off a third-party estate, the threat model here is Sameer's own phone rather than an unknown sender, and nothing has gone wrong. What makes it worth a row is that the remedy for the second half is probably one line in the systemd unit.

title: An atelier conversation moves between Guéridon and a tmux window with one tap or one keypress, and only one Claude ever holds it: the session baton

brief.badly: The model gets confused - gear slips in the environment that mess with the coherence of context or fail to give awareness of important transition characteristics, and I get confused too - not knowing in under 20s how to pick up the session where I was noodling something about XXX on surface YYY. brief.done: On the atelier, Sameer starts a conversation in Guéridon, presses R in the tmux window that appeared and carries on in the terminal, then taps it in Guéridon and carries on there, with the conversation intact both ways and never two Claude processes on one transcript
brief.how:
RULE: one conversation, one holder; a baton file per conversation (holder, pid, since) in the person's state dir. PHONE END = Guéridon's server. TERMINAL END = the atelier's claude shell function (ansible/roles/claude/files/atelier-cost-line.sh in ITV/mit-atelier, which already pins --session-id) plus a placeholder program 'atelier-baton wait <id>'. TAKE TO GUÉRIDON (tap a live terminal row): re-read the registry record (existing gdn-racuca check), if busy then WAIT for idle (default) or TAKE NOW = one Esc via tmux send-keys while status reads busy (measured 30 Sep on 2.1.285: Esc interrupts the turn and the running command, the process stays alive, idle within 3 s; SIGINT as a signal EXITS instead, so it cannot replace Esc); write the baton; SIGTERM (existing, graceful like /exit; SIGKILL after 3 s as now); the shell function in the window sees the baton and shows 'In Guéridon since HH:MM, press R to take it back'; start 'claude -p --resume <id>' with the usual flags. TAKE TO TERMINAL (press R): placeholder calls Guéridon's release endpoint on its local socket; Guéridon closes G's stdin when idle, updates the baton, marks the row 'In the terminal (tmux N)'; placeholder runs 'claude --resume <id>'. NEW SESSION IN GUÉRIDON: also 'tmux new-window -d -n <folder> atelier-baton wait <id>'. Transition note to the model at each move (terminal side via a SessionStart hook reading an env note, no extra turn; Guéridon side via [guéridon:system]). TO CHECK: SIGTERM while a permission prompt waits; G's permission posture (allow-list + default mode vs the home's auto) and what it does with an unlisted tool; the tmux server must never start inside Guéridon's unit (KillMode=control-group would take it down on restart); SIGTERM exit code is 143, so trust the baton, not the exit code.

PERMISSIONS (30 Sep): Guéridon has no permission chooser (none in client/) and forces --permission-mode default plus its own allow-list, so G behaves differently from the terminal Claude it took over. Sameer: 'maybe we just inherit the permission and align to the choice that was made earlier? Or just yolo it.' Facts for either: every user message in a transcript carries permissionMode (this session: bypassPermissions x134), so G can resume with the mode the conversation last ran in; and a headless session with no override takes the home's own default (the atelier probe reported bypassPermissions for Sameer's home). Proposal: inherit the transcript's last mode, else the home's default, by dropping the override. Also: buildSystemPrompt appends its own text to every G (host note, AskUserQuestion workaround, ~/.claude protection), which is exactly what made Sameer uneasy about Happy; keep it minimal and true, and it can double as the hand-over note.

DECIDED 2026-09-30 (Sameer: 'Inherit'): G resumes with the permission mode the conversation last ran in (the last permissionMode in its transcript); a new Guéridon session takes the home's own default. Remove the forced --permission-mode default.

30 Sep, both-sides inventory (page 'The Bounce', https://claude.ai/artifact/H9EiJXEGBhoGzXG3tt76bo, read from 600 tube transcripts): no transcript has ever changed entrypoint, so the bounce is new ground for Guéridon's replay. BUILD FIRST: (a) a pre-move check naming what the stop will end (registry status 'shell' = background shell running; turn_duration.pendingBackgroundAgentCount = pending agents; scheduled wakeups, monitors and queued messages are process-bound too) plus the waiting-prompt choice; (b) carry the TUI's half-typed draft (tmux capture-pane reads the input line); (c) the hand-over note, both directions, facts only, once per move, shown to Sameer as well; (d) the tmux placeholder says what is happening in Guéridon; (e) the atelier cost line misfires on a hand-over exit (label 'so far' or skip); (f) carry the model the way permissions are carried. MEASURE: is an enqueued-but-undelivered peer message or task notification lost at SIGTERM?

How do I start the build?'): on TUBE, in the dev checkout ~/repos/spm1001/gueridon, on a branch; never touch /opt/gueridon and never restart the production gueridon service (a restart kills every live Guéridon session on Sameer's phone); run a second Guéridon from the dev checkout on its own port for testing. title: Orphan reaper never fires — zombie bridge processes accumulate across restarts

brief.done: After a systemctl restart, ps aux | grep bridge.ts shows only the current bridge process and its immediate children. No accumulation across restarts. Memory stable.
brief.what: 1. Remove unlinkSync(SESSION_FILE) from shutdown() (line 1420) — the reaper already deletes the file at line 193 after consuming it 2. Verify reaper targets process groups not just the main CC PID (MCP server.py and esbuild children also leak) 3. Confirm SESSION_FILE path consistency — code uses sse-sessions.json (line 129) but original commit (6f154cb) referenced sessions.json 4. Add a safety net: on startup, kill any bridge.ts node processes in the cgroup that aren't the current PID
brief.why: KillMode=process (intentional) lets CC children survive bridge restart so sessions can resume. The reaper (reapOrphans) is supposed to clean them up on next boot. But shutdown() at bridge.ts:1420 calls unlinkSync(SESSION_FILE) BEFORE the new bridge starts — deleting the only record of which PIDs to reap. Result: 88 zombie bridge.ts processes consuming 6.1GB RSS on a 7.5GB machine after 4 days. Every systemctl restart makes it worse.

title: Field Report: CI red on main since 2026-08-30 (0ff9292) — session-index 'respects maxFiles newest-first' fails (expected 0 to be 1); still red on 6854ebc and 9ab54eb

brief.badly: we just end up with more complications in future (Sameer, campaign-open sheet 2026-09-13, verbatim)
brief.done: gh run list --repo spm1001/gueridon --branch main --limit 1 is success, and the fix names whether it was a flake or a regression.
brief.how:
gh run view --repo spm1001/gueridon --log-failed on the latest main run; reproduce with the vitest file in isolation and in the full suite; if it is an mtime-granularity flake in the fixture farm, make the fixture set distinct mtimes explicitly; if real, fix the newest-first cap.

REPRODUCED 2026-09-13 on tube (triage only — still open for a coding session). It is a FLAKE in the test, not a product regression: npx vitest run server/session-index.test.ts in isolation, 13 consecutive runs, 10 pass / 3 fail, every failure the same 'respects maxFiles newest-first' expected +0 to be 1. Identical runs seconds apart disagree, so 9ab54eb is not implicated. MECHANISM: session-index.ts:297 sorts candidates by b.mtimeMs - a.mtimeMs then slices to maxFiles. The fixture farm's beforeAll writes V4, V5_REMOTE, V4_COWORK and V4_EMPTY back-to-back with no utimes (only oldPath gets an explicit mtime), so they routinely share a millisecond; Array.sort is stable, so the tie-break falls through to readdir order, which is filesystem- not write-ordered. When V4_EMPTY wins the tie, maxFiles:1 keeps only that file, and V4_EMPTY is designed to be dropped (no human prompt, no title), so the scan returns 0 rows instead of 1. FIX: give each fixture an explicit distinct mtime via utimes in beforeAll; do not change scanRecentSessions, which is behaving correctly on a genuinely ambiguous input. A deterministic tie-break on path would be a reasonable second belt. Caveat: gh has no credentials in the mail-triage HOME, so this is all local on tube — the GitHub runs were not inspected.

CORRECTION to the run tally in the note above: the 13 runs were 9 pass / 4 fail (a first batch of 3 = 2 pass 1 fail, then a batch of 10 = 7 pass 3 fail), i.e. roughly a 30% failure rate, not 10/3. The mechanism and the conclusion are unchanged.

CORRECTION 2026-09-12 (review verifier): It is a flake, not a regression, and the mechanism is now known: session-index.ts:298 slices candidates to maxFiles BEFORE the head/substance filters at :310-320, and the fixture files are written within the same millisecond so they tie on mtime — whichever the sort puts first may be one the filters drop, giving 0. One-line fix: give the fixtures distinct mtimes via utimes (already imported at session-index.test.ts:2) or cap after filtering. Only 'push and confirm green' remains after that.
brief.what: 1. Reproduce. 2. Fix test or code. 3. Push; confirm gh run list shows green on main.
brief.why:
Found by the 2026-09-10 inbox census: gueridon's CI has been red on main since 6854ebc (2026-09-09 10:19Z), one failing test in server/session-index.test.ts (scanRecentSessions fixture farm → respects maxFiles newest-first: AssertionError expected +0 to be 1). Every future push to main will mail Sameer a GitHub 'Run failed' until it is green. The earlier 2026-08-30 pair (7ae8bb1 red, 140cc57 green, 0ff9292 red) suggests the same test may be order- or mtime-sensitive rather than a real regression — run it three times locally before changing product code.

CORRECTION 2026-09-11 (cold read of the infra handoff): red since 2026-08-30 on 0ff9292, not 2026-09-09 — this session first saw it on 6854ebc; the three failures the estate sweep counts are 0ff9292, 6854ebc, 9ab54eb.

done_note: FLAKE, not a regression. Fixed in two commits on main, both CI green (4a16185 run 34783607505; 3641242 run 34784113819). Mechanism as finally measured by the closing essayeur, correcting the card's earlier notes and the first commit message: ext4 mtimes move in 4 ms kernel ticks (HZ=250), so the fixture farm's five back-to-back writes usually tied and the empty/warmup fixture — written LAST — sometimes landed one tick later as the strictly newest file; maxFiles:1 then kept only it and the substance filters dropped it (0 rows). Not a same-millisecond tie broken by readdir order: the old fixtures still failed 5/20 with a path tie-break in the product sort, so the tie-break shipped in 4a16185 was reverted in 3641242 (Sameer's falsifier: no complications that fix nothing). The whole fix is the test: each fixture gets an explicit minutes-ago mtime via utimes, and the maxFiles test now asserts WHICH row survives. Before 9/12 (worker) and 18/20 (essayeur) isolated passes; after 15/15 (worker) and 20/20 (essayeur), full suite 759/759. Product code unchanged net. Converted from outcome to action to draw it down (one `bon convert`).

title: Closed sessions resume after bridge restart instead of starting fresh

brief.done: After /close + /exit + bridge restart, resolveSessionForFolder returns fresh session (not resume). Add test case: session with exit marker + stale handoff → outcome is 'fresh'.
brief.what: 1. ROOT CAUSE: isHandoffStale() in bridge-logic.ts compares handoff mtime vs .jsonl mtime. /close writes handoff mid-turn, then CC finishes the turn writing more events to .jsonl. The .jsonl mtime is always > handoff mtime after /close. isHandoffStale() returns true, handoff gets nulled, resolveSessionForFolder falls through to resume. 2. FIX OPTIONS: (a) In resolveSessionForFolder, check hasExitMarker BEFORE checking handoff staleness — exit marker is authoritative regardless of mtimes. (b) Tighten isHandoffStale to require a larger time delta (e.g. 5+ minutes) so same-turn writes don't trigger it. (c) Have the bridge auto-write exit marker in proc.on('exit') when a handoff exists for that session. Option (a) is simplest and most correct — exit marker means closed, full stop. 3. VERIFY: Check resolveSessionForFolder in bridge-logic.ts — the hasExit parameter exists but may be checked too late in the logic, after handoff staleness has already nulled the handoff signal.
brief.why: User runs /close then /exit. Bridge restarts. Instead of a fresh session, the old one resumes with 'bridge was restarted' message. This defeats the entire session lifecycle — handoffs become useless if the next session is just the old one resumed. Happened in production 2026-02-25.
